question_text: 'ध्यानं निर्विषयं मनः' का सम्बन्ध है
detailed_explanation:
**Answer: (2) सांख्यसूत्र.**

*Dhyānaṃ nirviṣayaṃ manaḥ* — "meditation is the mind free of objects" — is Sāṃkhya Sūtra 6.25 (Kapila's Sāṃkhya-pravacana sūtra).

Patañjali defines dhyāna differently: *tatra pratyayaikatānatā dhyānam* (YS 3.2), an unbroken flow of one cognition on the object. The "objectless" mind is closer to what Patañjali would call samādhi, which is why the line is a favourite trap.

question_text: 'सूर्याचन्द्रमसोर्योगो जीवात्मपरमात्मनोः' का निम्नलिखित में है।
detailed_explanation:
**Answer: (3) योगशिखोपनिषद्.**

The Yogaśikhā Upaniṣad (1.68–69) defines yoga as a set of unions: of prāṇa and apāna, of rajas and retas, **of sun and moon** (piṅgalā and iḍā), and **of jīvātman and paramātman**. *Evaṃ tu dvandva-jālasya saṃyogo yoga ucyate* — the joining of such pairs is called yoga.

The Kaṭha, Kaivalya and Maitrāyaṇī have their own definitions of yoga, but not this pairing.

question_text: सर जॉन मार्शल के अनुसार मोहनजोदड़ो में प्राप्त नरदेवता की मूर्ति है
detailed_explanation:
**Answer: (2) त्रिमुखी.**

Sir John Marshall described the Mohenjo-daro seal of a horned figure seated in a yogic posture, surrounded by animals, as **three-faced** (*trimukha*) and called it "proto-Śiva" (Paśupati). It is often cited as the earliest archaeological hint of yoga in the Indus civilisation.

The reading is debated by later archaeologists, but the exam asks for Marshall's description.

question_text: ईशोपनिषद् के अनुसार, साधक कब शोक व मोह रहित हो जाता है ?
options: सब प्राणियों के प्रति दया भावना से
सब मनुष्यों से प्रेम करने पर
सब मनुष्यों के प्रति करुणा की भावना से
सब प्राणियों के प्रति आत्मभाव भावना से
detailed_explanation:
**Answer: (4) सब प्राणियों के प्रति आत्मभाव.**

Īśa Upaniṣad 7: *yasmin sarvāṇi bhūtāny ātmaivābhūd vijānataḥ | tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka ekatvam anupaśyataḥ* — when, for the knower, all beings have become his own Self, what delusion or sorrow can there be for one who sees oneness?

Compassion, love and kindness (1–3) are good, but the verse names **seeing all beings as the Self** (verse 6 says the same) as what ends grief and delusion.

question_text: किस उपनिषद् में कहा गया है कि वेदान्तिक ज्ञान तथा शुद्ध अन्तःकरण वाले पुरुष अन्त में मुक्त हो जाते हैं?
detailed_explanation:
**Answer: (1) मुण्डकोपनिषद्.**

Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.2.6: *vedānta-vijñāna-suniścitārthāḥ saṃnyāsa-yogād yatayaḥ śuddha-sattvāḥ | te brahma-lokeṣu parāntakāle parāmṛtāḥ parimucyanti sarve* — ascetics who are certain of the meaning of Vedāntic knowledge and whose minds are purified through renunciation are all freed at the final end.

question_text: पतंजलि के अनुसार 'ध्यानहेयास्तद्वृत्तयः' का सम्बन्ध है
detailed_explanation:
**Answer: (4) क्लेशवृत्ति नाश से.**

YS 2.10–2.11: the subtle kleśas are destroyed by returning them to their source (*te pratiprasava-heyāḥ sūkṣmāḥ*), while their **active modifications** — the gross forms of the kleśas — are removed by meditation: ***dhyāna-heyās tad-vṛttayaḥ***.

"*Tad*" refers to the kleśas, not to the five citta-vṛttis of YS 1.6 (pramāṇa, viparyaya, vikalpa, nidrā, smṛti).

YS 4.29–4.30: for one who has no interest even in the highest knowledge, constant discrimination brings ***dharmamegha samādhi***, and ***tataḥ kleśa-karma-nivṛttiḥ*** — from that, kleśas and karma cease.

question_text: महर्षि पतंजलि के अनुसार, अन्तराय तथा विक्षेप-सहभुवः को दूर करने का उपाय क्या है?
detailed_explanation:
**Answer: (4) एकतत्त्वाभ्यास.**

YS 1.30 lists the nine antarāyas; 1.31 their companions (*vikṣepa-sahabhuvaḥ*: duḥkha, daurmanasya, aṅgamejayatva, śvāsa-praśvāsa); and 1.32 gives the remedy: ***tat-pratiṣedhārtham eka-tattvābhyāsaḥ*** — to prevent them, practise on one principle.

The four bhāvanās (1.33) and prāṇāyāma (1.34) follow as further means of steadying the mind, and abhyāsa-vairāgya (1.12) is the general method for nirodha.

question_text: जल व पंक से योगी के शरीर का संयोग किस कारण नहीं होता ?
detailed_explanation:
**Answer: (3) उदान वायु पर जय से.**

YS 3.39: ***udāna-jayāj jala-paṅka-kaṇṭakādiṣv asaṅga utkrāntiś ca*** — by mastery of udāna, the yogi does not touch water, mud, thorns and the like, and rises (or departs at will).

Mastery of samāna (YS 3.40) gives radiance (*jvalanam*). Udāna is the upward-moving vāyu, which is why its mastery gives lightness and levitation.

question_text: घेरण्ड संहिता के अनुसार, कपालरन्ध्र धौति किस धौति का प्रकार है?
detailed_explanation:
**Answer: (1) दन्तधौति.**

Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā 1.25: *danta-mūlaṃ jihvā-mūlaṃ randhraṃ ca karṇa-yugmayoḥ | kapāla-randhraṃ pañcaite danta-dhautir vidhīyate* — dantadhauti has five forms: the roots of the teeth, the root of the tongue, the two ear holes and **kapāla-randhra**.

GS 1.34–35 describe kapāla-randhra dhauti: rubbing the depression at the top of the forehead with the right thumb, which removes kapha and clears the nāḍīs.

This definition differs from Patañjali's five yamas, which is what the question tests.

**Answer: (3) पेन्क्रियाज.**

The pancreas is a mixed gland. detailed_explanation:
**Answer: (3) चार.**
